Issued at 241 PM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Afternoon RAP analysis features midlevel ridging extending from the 
Great Lakes through the Southern Plains, with troughing over the 
Intermountain West. At the surface, high pressure is centered over 
the St. Lawrence Seaway, extending ridging westward into the UP, 
with a surface low moving into the Northern Plains. Skies have been 
able to clear across most of our forecast area, though Day-Cloud 
Phase RGB still shows some fog and low stratus near the Lake 
Michigan shorelines and over far western Lake Superior. Amid light 
southerly flow, temperatures have been able to climb well into the 
60s and even low 70s over the far western UP (warmest in the 
southerly downsloping spots), while areas further eastward are 
peaking in the lower 60s. The Lake Michigan shorelines are 
struggling to get out of the 50s, but if we can finally see some 
clearing this afternoon, temperatures may be able to climb a couple 
more degrees. 

Tonight, the western low makes its way into Manitoba, with 
increasing south-southwest flow aloft and strengthening warm air 
advection into the UP. This brings an increase in cloud cover and 
perhaps some spotty showers to the western UP, though little to no 
accumulations are expected. Temperatures under cloudy skies only 
fall back into the mid 50s, while to the east, under partly cloudy 
skies, temperatures fall back into the mid to upper 40s. Some patchy 
fog is not out of the question across the eastern UP, but increasing 
winds and cloud cover should limit the extent of dense fog compared 
to previous nights. 

Southerly winds turn breezy Saturday, gusting to around 20-25mph for 
most of the area and in excess of 30mph over the higher terrain of 
the north-central UP and the downsloping areas near Superior. 
Temperatures stay elevated, peaking in the mid 60s to mid 70s over 
the western half of the UP and in the lower 60s over the east 
courtesy of flow off of Lake Michigan. Expect otherwise dry and 
mostly cloudy weather for the daytime hours, then chances for spotty 
rain showers return Saturday night as a cold front sweeps through. 
Rain lingers in the eastern UP into Sunday morning while the front 
exits eastward. Widespread totals of 0.10in or less are expected, 
though a few spots may be able to see slightly higher totals (20-30% 
chance for up to 0.15in). Winds turn westerly behind the front with 
cooler, near-normal temps peaking in the upper 40s to low 60s, 
coldest northwest and warmest south-central. Expect more breaks in 
the clouds into the afternoon as drier air works in, with soundings 
supporting a good dewpoint drop at least across the western UP. 
Dewpoints fall into the lower 20s and even upper teens over the 
interior-western UP, supporting minimum RH as low as 25-35%. Higher 
minimum RH in the upper 30s to mid 60s is expected in the Keweenaw 
and east. Winds look to remain under 15 mph at this time where RH is 
lowest (only a 10-30% chance for wind gusts exceeding 20 mph coupled 
with RH below 30%), limiting fire weather concerns. Will continue to 
monitor this period.

High pressure passes east over Ontario and the Great lakes Monday 
and Tuesday. Then flow aloft turns zonal, allowing for multiple 
shortwave troughs to track east next week into the following weekend. 
Guidance begins to struggle to resolve this pattern already by 
Tuesday night, but this likely sends a low pressure system just to 
the northwest of the Great Lakes mid to late next week. The 
shortwaves, low pressure system, and late week colder airmass 
yielding sufficient delta-Ts for lake effect precip keeps PoPs in 
most of the extended forecast. Otherwise, temps return near normal 
in the wake of the cold front on Sunday peaking in the 40s to low 
50s Monday and Tuesday. Temps Monday night settle into the 20s to 
mid 30s, coldest interior west. Southerly flow returning for 
Wednesday and Thursday warm temps into the 50s with lows in the 30s 
and 40s.
